trigger: Wayfinder validation crosses Python and PowerShell, uses an isolated venv, or reports a dependency available in one command but missing in a nested validator.

steps.action: Resolve one Python 3 interpreter through Resolve-WayfinderPython.ps1. Explicit PythonPath wins; invalid explicit/override bindings fail closed.
Print source, canonical sys.executable path, and version before dependency checks.
Check jsonschema 4.26.x with the bound interpreter only.
Run runtime-binding, Wayfinder semantic, and contribution Python validators with the bound interpreter.
Run PowerShell validators while passing the same -PythonPath into every nested Wayfinder validator.
Run public-plan, agent-documentation, operational-harness, and diff-hygiene checks after focused validators pass.
Resolve canonical manifest/report paths from the scoped artifact registry; never invent a report path.
Record exact head, interpreter binding, validator outcomes, proof ceiling, and first unresolved live gate.

failureRules: Do not install a missing dependency into a different interpreter than the one the validator will execute.
Do not silently fall back when -PythonPath or ASB_WAYFINDER_PYTHON was explicitly supplied but is invalid.
Do not treat requested-path versus canonical sys.executable string differences as failure when the bound interpreter executes successfully.
Do not continue to broader validation after an owning validator fails.
proofCeiling: Proves deterministic interpreter continuity and repository validators only. It does not prove provider, tracker, HITL, deployment, or destination runtime behavior.
